correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the weighted inequality to \(F+(1-c)R\ge0\) using the source's finite-support right inverse and hence dense range. A vector orthogonal to the finite-rank range forces \(c\le1\). The rank-one vectors are linearly independent because their numerator polynomials are monic of distinct degrees, so \(F\ge0\) is equivalent to nonnegativity of every explicit coefficient \(\lambda_{m,r}(\alpha)\). Their product formula then gives the stated integer/large-parameter classification exactly. The critical nonstandard identities were read in the focal full text; no numerical experiment enters the argument.

value.rationale: The focal paper explicitly leaves its quantitative constant nonoptimal. The coefficient \(c_m(\alpha)\) is the natural sharp invariant attached to that weighted estimate, and identifying exactly when it attains the universal ceiling \(1\) gives a structural phase diagram rather than a routine numerical improvement. It recovers the older order-two and order-three parameter regimes as the exact unit-strength regimes and explains what changes quantitatively on the newly settled noninteger bands.
